obligation: Retail and foodservice customer notice
trigger: Any event that could affect product safety, lot traceability, or committed volumes
deadline: Within 24 hours
notify: Each affected customer's food safety and supply contacts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - about 76% of revenue under these agreements
clock_starts: Declaration of a severity-1 incident that touches packing, cold chain, traceability, or shipping
owner: Vice President, Sales and Customer Operations

obligation: SL-1 grower data platform client notice
citation: SL-1 client agreements (contract; SOC 2 system description commitments)
trigger: Incident affecting SL-1 client data or availability beyond the service level
deadline: Within 72 hours of confirming the incident; status updates every 24 hours until restored
applies_at_this_tier: Yes
clock_starts: Confirmation that SL-1 data or service is affected

obligation: SL-2 grower packing and traceability client notice
trigger: Incident affecting lot codes, traceability data, or cooling records for grower produce at the hubs
deadline: Within 24 hours
applies_at_this_tier: Yes
clock_starts: Confirmation that hub lot or traceability data is affected

obligation: State breach notice to individuals (each state of residence)
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of state residents (definitions vary by state)
deadline: Varies by state (for example "without unreasonable delay" or a fixed number of days)
applies_at_this_tier: Always check. Apply the law of each state where affected individuals reside (FL, GA, SC, NC workers and subscribers; seasonal workers housed in other states)
clock_starts: Varies by state (usually discovery or determination of the breach)
owner: Chief Privacy Officer with outside counsel

obligation: State attorney general or regulator notice
trigger: Breach above a state-set count of residents
deadline: Varies by state
notify: State attorney general or designated regulator
applies_at_this_tier: Check each state with affected residents

obligation: State consumer reporting agency notice
trigger: Notices above a state-set count
deadline: Varies by state
applies_at_this_tier: Check each state with affected residents

obligation: State third-party agent (vendor) notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: A vendor that maintains personal information for the company has a breach
deadline: Varies by state
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - payroll provider, FMIS vendor, e-commerce vendor

obligation: Florida notice to individuals (worked example)
trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents (includes Social Security, passport, and financial account numbers)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred; 15 more days only with good cause given in writing to the Department within 30 days (501.171(3)(a))
notify: Each affected individual in Florida, by mail or email, with the minimum content in 501.171(4)(e)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred

obligation: Florida law enforcement delay (worked example)
trigger: A federal, state, or local law enforcement agency determines notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Notice delayed for the period in the agency's written request (may be extended or revoked in writing)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if requested

obligation: Florida no-notice determination (worked example)
trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the company reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Document in writing, keep at least 5 years, and provide to the Department within 30 days after the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Only if the determination is made (unlikely for stolen payroll and passport files)

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs (worked example)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination (no extension for this notice)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs, with the content in 501.171(3)(b)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Floridians (likely: most of the workforce is in Florida)
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies (worked example)
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (15 U.S.C. 1681a(p)): timing, distribution, and content of the notices
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 1,000 notified at once
clock_starts: Decision to notify more than 1,000 individuals

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to the company (worked example)
trigger: Breach of a system maintained by a vendor acting as third-party agent
deadline: Vendor notifies the company no later than 10 days after determining the breach; the company then gives the (3) and (4) notices
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - payroll provider, FMIS vendor, e-commerce vendor

obligation: SEC materiality determination
trigger: Cybersecurity incident discovered that could be material, including an OT outage (17 CFR 229.106(a) definition of information systems)
deadline: Without unreasonable delay after discovery of the incident
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SEC registrant

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 filing
trigger: Company determines a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: Within 4 business days after the materiality determination
notify: SEC (public filing to investors), with Inline XBRL tagging (Item 1.05(b))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: SEC filing delay on Attorney General determination
trigger: U.S. Attorney General determines disclosure poses a substantial risk to national security or public safety and notifies the SEC in writing
deadline: Delay up to 30 days, then up to 30 more, then up to 60 more in extraordinary circumstances (national security), as the Attorney General determines
notify: SEC (through the Attorney General's written notice)
applies_at_this_tier: Only on the Attorney General's determination

obligation: SEC Form 8-K amendment for missing information
trigger: Information required by Item 1.05(a) was not determined or unavailable at filing
deadline: Within 4 business days after the information is determined or becomes available
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the first filing had open items
clock_starts: Determination or availability of the missing information

obligation: SEC annual cybersecurity disclosure
trigger: Annual report on Form 10-K
deadline: With the annual report
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: Insider trading blackout
trigger: Disclosure committee convenes on a possibly material incident
deadline: Immediately when the committee convenes
notify: Committee members, responders with knowledge, executives
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (2021-09-21); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Any ransom payment is considered
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: All U.S. persons. Strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

obligation: Law enforcement report (voluntary)
trigger: Ransomware or extortion
deadline: As soon as practicable (company practice: within 24 hours of declaration)
notify: FBI field office or IC3; CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes (voluntary)

obligation: CIRCIA incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after a ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: NOT YET REQUIRED: final rule not published as of 2026-09-25 (reporting is voluntary until then). As proposed, the company would be covered through the size criterion (above the SBA size standard)
clock_starts: Reasonable belief that a covered incident occurred (proposed)

obligation: Cyber insurance notice
trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy (the policy requires notice as soon as practicable; panel firms must be used to keep coverage)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: Acquirer and payment processor notice
citation: Acquirer merchant agreement (contract); PCI DSS; Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0 (effective 2026-06-25), Section A.1.1
trigger: Suspected compromise of the produce box e-commerce or payment page
deadline: Per acquirer agreement (time not set in this sample; immediately on suspicion). Whatever the agreement says, Visa's rules require the compromise to be reported to Visa within 3 calendar days of suspicion or confirmation, through the acquirer (What To Do If Compromised v10.0, A.1.1)
applies_at_this_tier: Only if the e-commerce SaaS or hosted payment page is involved (card data is not on company systems)
verified: n/a (contract term not set); true (Visa clock)
owner: Vice President, Sales and Customer Operations

obligation: Produce Safety records available to FDA during an outage
trigger: FDA requests records during or after the outage
deadline: Offsite records retrieved and provided within 24 hours of the request
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - covered farm
owner: Chief Food Safety and Quality Officer

obligation: Food Traceability Rule records available to FDA
trigger: FDA requests traceability records (outbreak, recall, or other public health threat)
deadline: Within 24 hours of the request (electronic sortable spreadsheet for 1.1455(c)(3) requests); FDA will not enforce before 2028-07-20
applies_at_this_tier: Yes from 2028-07-20 (readiness now; P03)

obligation: H-2A hours and earnings statements during an outage
trigger: Each payday, including during an outage
deadline: On or before each payday
notify: Each H-2A worker (and workers in corresponding employment)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - H-2A employer
owner: Director of H-2A and Labor Compliance

obligation: H-2A earnings records available for inspection
trigger: Notice from the Department of Labor (or a worker's request) during or after the outage
deadline: Records kept centrally must be available within 72 hours following notice
notify: Department of Labor; the worker or the worker's designated representative
applies_at_this_tier: Yes
clock_starts: Notice from the Secretary or a duly authorized representative
owner: Director of H-2A and Labor Compliance

obligation: Worker Protection Standard application and hazard information display
trigger: Pesticide application during the outage
deadline: Displayed no later than 24 hours after the end of each application
notify: Workers and handlers (central display at the establishment)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - agricultural employer

obligation: Reportable Food Registry
trigger: Responsible party determines an article of food is a reportable food
deadline: As soon as practicable, no later than 24 hours after the determination
applies_at_this_tier: No - the duty falls on the responsible party that registers a food facility; the company registers none. If an incident could have adulterated product (for example, fertigation tampering), tell customers within 24 hours (contract) so the registered facilities downstream can make their own determination
owner: Chief Food Safety and Quality Officer

obligation: FAA small UAS safety event report
trigger: A drone operation causes serious injury, loss of consciousness, or property damage over $500 (for example, a drone flown with tampered software)
deadline: No later than 10 calendar days after the operation
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if a drone event meets the criteria

obligation: Federal contract reports (covered telecommunications; Kaspersky covered article)
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d); FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Covered telecommunications equipment or a covered article found in use or delivered
deadline: 52.204-25(d): within 1 business day, then 10 business days; 52.204-23(c): within 3 business days, then 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - no federal prime contracts or subcontracts since 2024
